1	# Agent Session Retrospective Playbook
2	
3	**Version:** 1.0 (2026-07-14) · **Portable:** yes — this file plus a `LOCAL.md`
4	adaptation is everything a fresh agent needs to run one retrospective round in
5	any project, under any coding-agent runtime.
6	
7	## Purpose
8	
9	Mine past agent sessions for evidence about **how the human and their coding
10	agents work together** — not about any one project. Output: cumulative,
11	evidence-backed recommendations that reduce friction and increase velocity.
12	
13	Improvement dimensions (the finding taxonomy — tag every finding with one):
14	
15	| Tag | Meaning |
16	|---|---|
17	| `prompting-pattern` | Phrasings/structures in the human's asks that helped or hurt |
18	| `under-specified` | Agent guessed wrong because the ask lacked a constraint |
19	| `over-specified` | Constraints that wasted effort or blocked better solutions |
20	| `missing-skill` | A reusable procedure that should exist but doesn't |
21	| `detrimental-skill` | A skill/command that fired and made things worse |
22	| `missing-tool` | Capability gap (script, MCP server, permission, hook) |
23	| `bad-tool` | A tool that exists but misbehaves |
24	| `mishandled-tool` | Tool is fine; the agent used it wrong |
25	| `tokenomics` | Context/token waste: re-reads, giant outputs, compaction churn, re-priming |
26	| `model-task-mismatch` | Wrong tier for the work; escalation loops; redone delegations |
27	| `process` | Workflow friction: unclosed sessions, stranded work, duplicate tracking |
28	| `environment` | Sandbox, OS, auth, path quirks |
29	| `win` | A pattern that worked well — candidate to amplify/standardize |
30	
31	## Units
32	
33	- **Session** — one top-level interactive conversation with an agent runtime.
34	  Sub-agent runs (spawned subagents, `codex exec` calls made *by* a session)
35	  are evidence *within* their parent session, not sessions themselves.
36	- **Batch** — exactly **5 substantive sessions**, assessed together.
37	- **Round** — one execution of Phases 1–4 on one batch. A round is sized to
38	  fit one agent session; the state files make the exercise resumable forever.
39	- **Campaign** — all sessions for one (project × runtime) scope.
40	
41	## State files (all in this `retro/` directory)
42	
43	| File | Tracked in git? | Contents |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| `PLAYBOOK.md` | yes | this procedure (portable) |
46	| `LOCAL.md` | yes | per-repo adaptation: paths, tracker wiring, commit protocol |
47	| `ledger.tsv` | yes | one row per known session: scope, id, date, size, status, batch |
48	| `findings.md` | yes | cumulative findings register — **the** long-lived output |
49	| `batches/round-NN.md` | yes | one-page synthesis per round |
50	| `digests/*.md` | **no** (gitignored) | per-session digests; may quote transcripts → never publish |
51	
52	**Privacy rule:** transcripts can contain secrets, tokens, and private paths.
53	Digests stay untracked. Anything that IS committed (`findings.md`, `batches/`)
54	must be redaction-checked: no credentials, no long verbatim transcript dumps,
55	quotes ≤ 25 words. This matters doubly in public repos.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Phase 0 — Data source map (once per machine/runtime)
60	
61	Locate the session stores. Verified layouts as of 2026-07-14:
62	
63	**Claude Code** — `~/.claude/projects/<slugified-cwd>/*.jsonl`, one file per
64	session (top-level files only; subdirectories hold tool results/sidechains).
65	JSONL `type` field: `user`, `assistant`, `system`, plus noise types
66	(`attachment`, `file-history-snapshot`, `queue-operation`, …). Assistant lines
67	carry `message.model` and full `message.usage` token breakdowns.
68	
69	**Codex CLI** — `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-<ts>-<id>.jsonl`.
70	First line is `session_meta`; filter on `.payload.originator` / `.payload.source`:
71	`codex-tui`+`cli` = interactive session (retro unit); `codex_exec`+`exec` =
72	delegated run (attach to parent by cwd+timestamp); `source` containing
73	`subagent` = spawned child (attach to `parent_thread_id`).
74	
75	**Amp** — `~/.local/share/amp/threads/T-*.json`, one JSON per thread with
76	`messages[]` (role, content, `usage.model`).
77	
78	**Any other runtime / fallback evidence** (works even with no transcripts):
79	git log trailers (`Agent-Signature:` here), issue-tracker history, PR/commit
80	timestamps vs session dates, `reports/` retro-docs.
81	
82	## Phase 1 — Inventory & batching (mechanical, ~zero model tokens)
83	
84	1. Enumerate sessions for the campaign scope into `ledger.tsv`
85	   (see LOCAL.md for ready-made commands). Columns:
86	   `scope  runtime  session_id  started  size_kb  status  batch  note`
87	   Status values: `pending | skipped-trivial | skipped-subagent | skipped-inflight | digested | synthesized`.
88	2. Filter substantive: mark `< 100 KB` (Claude/Codex) or `< 8 messages` (Amp)
89	   as `skipped-trivial` unless a note says otherwise. Mark sub-agent runs
90	   `skipped-subagent`. Mark the currently-running session `skipped-inflight`.
91	3. Order **newest-first** — recent sessions reflect current tooling, so their
92	   findings are actionable immediately; old sessions mostly reveal already-
93	   fixed friction (see stop rule 3).
94	4. Take the next 5 `pending` rows → that's this round's batch. Assign batch
95	   number in the ledger.
96	
97	## Phase 2 — Per-session digest (cheap model tier)
98	
99	**2a. Strip mechanically first** (jq/scripting, zero model tokens). Keep: user
100	text, assistant text, tool names + first ~120 chars of input, error results,
101	model + output-token usage, timestamps. Drop: full tool results, thinking,
102	attachments, snapshots. Verified compression on a real 1.5 MB Claude Code
103	transcript: → 88 KB ≈ 22 k tokens (~17×). Recipes per runtime in LOCAL.md.
104	
105	**2b. One digest agent per stripped transcript** — cheapest adequate tier
106	(they read ~25 k tokens, apply a fixed rubric, write ~1–2 k). Run the 5 in
107	parallel if the runtime allows. Each writes `digests/<runtime>-<id8>.md`:
108	
109	```markdown
110	# <runtime>/<id8> — <date> — <project>
111	meta: model(s)+effort | wall-clock span | msg count | output-tokens total
112	task: what was asked (1–3 lines; note if the ask evolved mid-session)
113	outcome: done-verified | done | partial | abandoned | unclear
114	  evidence: commits/PRs/issues/files produced, or user's closing sentiment
115	effectiveness: 1–5
116	  5 done+verified, little steering, cost ∝ task · 4 done, minor friction
117	  3 done but heavy steering/redo loops · 2 partial handback · 1 abandoned/wrong
118	friction:              # 0..n items, THE payload
119	- [tag] [H|M|L] what happened — evidence: "≤25-word quote" (who bore the cost: human|agent|both)
120	wins:
121	- [win] what worked and why it worked
122	delegation: subagents/exec runs spawned; tier fit right/over/under; redos
123	user-style: phrasings that produced clean runs or confusion (short quotes)
124	recs: 0–3 candidate recommendations, each tagged
125	```
126	
127	Digest agents must quote *evidence*, not impressions — a finding without a
128	quote or a concrete event is an impression and gets marked `[weak]`.
129	High-signal markers to hunt for: user interruptions and corrections
130	("no, I meant", "stop", "again?"), permission-prompt stalls and denials,
131	tool-error retry loops, compaction events, questions the agent asked that the
132	opening prompt should have answered, redone subagent work, sessions that end
133	without closing protocol, apologies.
134	
135	## Phase 3 — Batch synthesis (smart model tier — judgment work)
136	
137	Inputs: the 5 digests + current `findings.md`. Steps:
138	
139	1. For each friction/win item: **match against existing findings** — if it
140	   recurs, append the new evidence line and bump the count; else add a new
141	   `candidate` finding.
142	2. **Fixed-since check:** for older findings, note whether this batch's
143	   (newer or older) sessions show the friction absent after some change —
144	   move toward `verified-fixed`.
145	3. Write `batches/round-NN.md` (≤ 1 page): sessions covered, effectiveness
146	   scores, new findings, recurrences, promotions proposed, and **process
147	   notes on the retro itself** (rubric gaps, digest quality — this playbook
148	   is also under retrospection; bump its version when you change it).
149	4. Update `ledger.tsv` statuses.
150	
151	`findings.md` entry format:
152	
153	```markdown
154	### F-NNN · [tag] short title
155	- status: candidate → recurring → promoted → verified-fixed | retired
156	- sightings: N — <runtime>/<id8> (date): "quote"; …
157	- cost: who pays and roughly how much (turns, tokens, wall-clock, mood)
158	- recommendation: the specific change, and where it would live
159	- promoted-to: <link/path once acted on> · verify-by: what future sessions should show
160	```
161	
162	## Phase 4 — Promotion (recommendations → durable change)
163	
164	A finding is **actionable** at ≥ 2 independent sightings (or 1 with high
165	severity). Route by kind:
166	
167	| Finding kind | Durable home |
168	|---|---|
169	| prompting pattern (human side) | "Prompt cookbook" section at top of `findings.md` |
170	| agent behavior rule | CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / runtime memory (`bd remember`, auto-memory) |
171	| missing / broken skill | create or fix the skill; note the trigger phrase |
172	| permissions / hooks / config | runtime settings (e.g. allowlists, SessionStart hooks) |
173	| model–task matching | the repo's delegation-tier table |
174	| missing tool | script it, adopt it, or file it in the issue tracker |
175	
176	Every promotion gets a tracked task in the project's issue tracker **and** a
177	`verify-by` line — the closed loop: a later round must confirm the friction
178	actually disappeared, else the finding reopens.
179	
180	## Phase 5 — Iterate
181	
182	Run rounds until a stop rule fires:
183	
184	1. **Saturation** — two consecutive rounds add zero new findings (only
185	   recurrences): switch to maintenance cadence (one round per ~20 new
186	   sessions, or monthly).
187	2. **Promotion backlog** — > ~10 unpromoted actionable findings: stop mining,
188	   start promoting. Mining faster than fixing is waste.
189	3. **Staleness horizon** — sessions predating the last major process overhaul:
190	   mine only for `prompting-pattern`/`user-style` signal (human habits age
191	   slowly; tooling friction findings from that era are mostly already fixed).
192	
193	**Cost per round** (measured basis): 5 stripped transcripts ≈ 110–125 k tokens
194	read on the cheap tier + ~10 k digest output; synthesis reads ~15 k on the
195	smart tier. Budget ≈ 150–250 k tokens/round all-in. If a second vendor's CLI
196	is available (e.g. Codex from a Claude session), digesting there is free
197	quota relief — log it, since it bypasses budget accounting.
198	
199	## Porting to a new project or runtime
200	
201	1. Copy `PLAYBOOK.md` into `<project>/retro/` (or point at a central copy —
202	   a personal coordination repo is the natural home, and a **single shared
203	   `findings.md`** across projects is where cross-project patterns emerge;
204	   per-project you only need a ledger and digests).
205	2. Write `LOCAL.md`: session-store paths for the runtimes used there, strip
206	   recipes, tracker wiring, commit/close protocol, model tiers available.
207	3. Seed `ledger.tsv` (Phase 1) and open a standing "run next retro round"
208	   task in that project's tracker so cold-start agents find it.
209	
210	**Round entry point (give this to any agent):**
211	> Run one retrospective round per `retro/PLAYBOOK.md` + `retro/LOCAL.md`.
212	> Pick the next batch from `retro/ledger.tsv`, execute Phases 2–4, update the
213	> state files, and close per LOCAL.md.
214

1	# LOCAL.md — mybd adaptation of the retro playbook
2	
3	This repo (maphew/mybd, **public**) is the coordination home for the
4	cross-project retro campaign: the shared `findings.md` lives here even when
5	the sessions under review belong to other projects. Redaction rules from
6	PLAYBOOK.md apply with extra force — the repo is public.
7	
8	## Campaign inventory (as of 2026-07-14, this machine)
9	
10	| Scope | Substantive sessions | Notes |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| mybd × Claude Code | 15 of 19 (≥100 KB) | seeded in `ledger.tsv` |
13	| fauxcasa × Claude Code | ~23 (127 MB store) | seed when campaign starts |
14	| agentsview, mdo, oracle-batch3 × Claude Code | ~12 | " |
15	| all × Amp | 269 of 386 threads ≥ 8 msgs | " |
16	| all × Codex (interactive `codex-tui`/`cli` only) | TBD — most of the 452 rollouts are `codex_exec` delegate runs | " |
17	
18	≈ 12+ rounds of 5 for Claude Code alone. Expect stop-rule 1 or 2 to fire
19	well before exhaustion — that is the design, not a failure.
20	
21	## Inventory / strip recipes (verified 2026-07-14)
22	
23	Claude Code — seed ledger rows for a project store:
24	
25	```bash
26	STORE=~/.claude/projects/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd   # slug = cwd with / → -
27	for f in "$STORE"/*.jsonl; do
28	  id=$(basename "$f" .jsonl)
29	  start=$(jq -r 'select(.timestamp != null) | .timestamp' "$f" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
30	  kb=$(( $(stat -c%s "$f") / 1024 ))
31	  printf 'mybd\tclaude-code\t%s\t%s\t%s\tpending\t\t\n' "$id" "${start:0:10}" "$kb"
32	done >> ledger.tsv
33	```
34	
35	Claude Code — strip a transcript (1.5 MB → 88 KB ≈ 22 k tokens, measured):
36	
37	```bash
38	jq -c '
39	  select(.type=="user" or .type=="assistant" or .type=="system") |
40	  if .type=="user" then
41	    {t:"u", ts:.timestamp,
42	     txt: (if (.message.content|type)=="string" then .message.content
43	           else ([.message.content[]? | select(.type=="text") | .text] | join("\n")) end | .[0:2500]),
44	     err: [.message.content | if type=="string" then empty
45	           else .[]? | select(.type=="tool_result" and (.is_error==true)) | ((.content|tostring)[0:300]) end]}
46	  elif .type=="assistant" then
47	    {t:"a", ts:.timestamp, m:.message.model, out:.message.usage.output_tokens,
48	     txt: ([.message.content[]? | select(.type=="text") | .text] | join("\n") | .[0:1500]),
49	     tools: [.message.content[]? | select(.type=="tool_use") | (.name + ":" + ((.input|tostring)[0:120]))]}
50	  else
51	    {t:"s", ts:.timestamp, s: ((.content // (.message|tostring) // "")[0:250])}
52	  end' "$SESSION.jsonl" > digests/work/"$ID".stripped.jsonl
53	```
54	
55	Codex — classify rollouts (only `codex-tui` + `cli` are retro units):
56	
57	```bash
58	find ~/.codex/sessions -name '*.jsonl' | while read -r f; do
59	  head -1 "$f" | jq -r --arg f "$f" \
60	    '.payload | "\(.originator)/\(if (.source|type)=="string" then .source else "subagent" end)\t\($f)"'
61	done | grep '^codex-tui/cli' | cut -f2
62	```
63	
64	Amp — thread inventory: `jq '{id, msgs:(.messages|length), title}' ~/.local/share/amp/threads/T-*.json`
65	(strip = keep `role`, text content, `usage.model`; drop tool payloads).
66	
67	## Execution wiring (this repo's rules apply)
68	
69	- **Track rounds in bd.** Epic + one open "run retro round N" task at all
70	  times — that keeps the campaign on the `bd ready` cold-start path. Close
71	  round N's bead and open round N+1's at session close.
72	- **Digest agents (Phase 2b):** Claude `haiku`/low effort, or
73	  `scripts/codex-agent scout -o digests/<name>.md "<rubric + stripped file path>" </dev/null`
74	  for quota relief (Codex tokens bypass `budget.spent()` — log each call).
75	  The 5 digests may run in parallel: read-only inputs, disjoint outputs, no
76	  bd/dolt involvement. Everything touching bd stays serial.
77	- **Synthesis (Phase 3):** stays in the orchestrator session (smart tier) —
78	  it is judgment work over ~15 k tokens; delegating it wastes more than it saves.
79	- **Workflow tool:** pre-authorized here (AGENTS.md standing opt-in). A round
80	  fits `pipeline(batch, strip→digest)` with a barrier before synthesis.
81	  Default budget +200 k self-enforced.
82	- **Commits:** from a worktree under `.worktrees/mybd/`, ff-merge to main,
83	  standard Agent-Signature trailer, push (team-maintainer profile). Track
84	  `findings.md`, `batches/`, `ledger.tsv`, playbook/LOCAL edits. Never track
85	  `digests/` (see `.gitignore`) — transcript quotes stay local.
86	- **Session close:** `/session-close` as usual; the round's batch report is
87	  the deliverable and must be reachable from the open round-N+1 bead.
88	
89	## Round entry point (paste into a fresh session here)
90	
91	> Run one retrospective round per `retro/PLAYBOOK.md` + `retro/LOCAL.md`:
92	> claim the open retro bead, take the next 5 pending ledger rows, strip +
93	> digest (cheap tier / codex scout), synthesize into `retro/findings.md` and
94	> `retro/batches/round-NN.md` in-session, promote anything actionable, update
95	> the ledger, close per repo protocol, and open the next round's bead.
96

#!/bin/bash
# Mechanical transcript strip for retro digests. Zero model tokens.
set -u
OUT="$(dirname "$0")/stripped"
mkdir -p "$OUT"

CSTORE=~/.claude/projects/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd

strip_claude() { # $1 = session id
  local f="$CSTORE/$1.jsonl" id8="${1:0:8}"
  jq -c '
    select(.type=="user" or .type=="assistant" or .type=="system") |
    if .type=="user" then
      {t:"u", ts:.timestamp,
       txt: (if (.message.content|type)=="string" then .message.content
             else ([.message.content[]? | select(.type=="text") | .text] | join("\n")) end | .[0:2500]),
       err: [.message.content | if type=="string" then empty
             else .[]? | select(.type=="tool_result" and (.is_error==true)) | ((.content|tostring)[0:300]) end]} |
      select(.txt != "" or (.err|length) > 0)
    elif .type=="assistant" then
      {t:"a", ts:.timestamp, m:.message.model, out:.message.usage.output_tokens,
       txt: ([.message.content[]? | select(.type=="text") | .text] | join("\n") | .[0:1500]),
       tools: [.message.content[]? | select(.type=="tool_use") | (.name + ":" + ((.input|tostring)[0:120]))]}
    else
      {t:"s", ts:.timestamp, s: ((.content // (.message|tostring) // "")[0:250])}
    end' "$f" > "$OUT/claude-$id8.jsonl" 2>>"$OUT/strip-errors.log"
}

strip_codex() { # $1 = rollout path
  local f="$1" base id8
  base=$(basename "$f" .jsonl); id8="${base: -8}"
  jq -c '
    if .type=="session_meta" then {t:"meta", cwd:.payload.cwd, cli:.payload.cli_version, inst:(.payload.instructions|tostring|.[0:0])}
    elif .type=="turn_context" then {t:"ctx", model:.payload.model, effort:.payload.effort, sandbox:(.payload.sandbox_policy|tostring|.[0:60])}
    elif .type=="response_item" and .payload.type=="message" and .payload.role=="user" then
      {t:"u", ts:.timestamp, txt:([.payload.content[]? | .text // empty] | join("\n") | .[0:2500])} | select(.txt|test("<permissions|<environment_context|<user_instructions|AGENTS.md")|not)
    elif .type=="response_item" and (.payload.type=="agent_message" or (.payload.type=="message" and .payload.role=="assistant")) then
      {t:"a", ts:.timestamp, txt:(( .payload.message // ([.payload.content[]? | .text // empty]|join("\n")) ) | tostring | .[0:1500])}
    elif .type=="response_item" and (.payload.type=="function_call" or .payload.type=="custom_tool_call") then
      {t:"call", ts:.timestamp, n:.payload.name, a:((.payload.arguments // .payload.input)|tostring|.[0:150])}
    elif .type=="response_item" and (.payload.type=="function_call_output" or .payload.type=="custom_tool_call_output") then
      ( (.payload.output|tostring) as $o |
        {t:"out", ts:.timestamp, o:($o|.[0:250])} | select($o | test("exit_code\":0|\"output\":\"\"") | not) )
    elif .type=="event_msg" and .payload.type=="token_count" then
      {t:"tok", total:(.payload.info.total_token_usage.total_tokens // null)} | select(.total != null)
    elif .type=="event_msg" and (.payload.type=="error" or .payload.type=="stream_error" or .payload.type=="warning") then
      {t:"err", ts:.timestamp, e:(.payload|tostring|.[0:300])}
    else empty end' "$f" > "$OUT/codex-$id8.jsonl" 2>>"$OUT/strip-errors.log"
}

# Session machinery retro, 2026-07-22 → 07-25 — Claude second opinion

**Scope:** all agent sessions on this machine in the last 3 days, across Claude
Code, Codex CLI, Amp, and Kilocode. Question: *is the machinery running well —
not what the sessions did, but how.*

**Method:** independent of (and deliberately parallel to) the Codex-side audit
committed earlier today
([cross-runtime retrospective](2026-07-25-cross-runtime-session-machinery-retrospective.md),
bead `mybd-lq8i.2`). This pass digested **every substantive session
individually** — 17 Claude + 8 Codex interactive transcripts, mechanically
stripped (~17×) then digested by 16 parallel haiku agents against the
`retro/PLAYBOOK.md` rubric — plus mechanical forensics on the pr-babysit patrol
log, verify queue, Amp/Codex logs, and repo hygiene. Digests are in
`retro/digests/` (untracked by policy); recurring findings were registered in
`retro/findings.md` (F-001…F-010) and the ledger updated. A comparison against
the Codex report closes this document.

## Bottom line

The machinery is healthy and — the strongest signal in the window —
**self-correcting**. Effectiveness across 25 digested sessions: Claude mean
≈ 4.4/5 (17 sessions), Codex mean ≈ 3.75/5 (8 sessions); no abandoned work, no
data loss, every incident diagnosed in-session. The window's one hard process
failure (a PR merged onto red CI by one of five parallel sessions on 07-24)
produced, within hours, the pr-babysit patrol — which by 07-25 every session
used correctly.

Four things deserve fixing or tuning, in priority order:

1. **pr-babysit treats transient GitHub states as terminal** — new, not in the
   Codex report. 18 merge tails are currently stranded in `merge-blocked`.
2. **Delegation debris starves the host** — two same-day hard incidents
   (fd exhaustion; /tmp quota) with the enforcement gap still open.
3. **Codex orchestration burns tokens on `wait_agent` polling** — up to ~10M
   tokens of idle waiting in a single session.
4. **`bd --json` output-shape inconsistency** — small, but it taxed 4+ sessions
   and it taxed *this* session too.

Amp remains the observability weak point (corroborating the Codex report — I
verified `amp.dangerouslyAllowAll: true` directly). Kilocode: no activity since
January (CLI) / March (extension); drop it from audit scope until it returns.

## What is working well (keep, don't touch)

- **Cross-vendor review pairs are the standout pattern.** In six sessions the
  Claude and Codex reviewers found *largely disjoint real defects* on the same
  diff — e.g. 5 CI-integrity issues on PR 5004, a P1 TOCTOU on PR 5042, 5 FATAL
  findings on the psxg.2 design v1, 6 findings on workspace-gate. Every pairing
  paid for itself. Already institutionalized in PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES.md.
- **The zero-token control plane earns its keep.** Verify queue: all recent
  candidates passed, logs tidy (104 KB). Patrol: 6 PRs merged autonomously in
  the window while correctly refusing to merge onto red main — stop-the-line
  held twice (07-24 and 07-25 red-main incidents). Worktree discipline: no
  stashes, no gone branches, isolation used by default.
- **Session-close protocol is real.** Multiple textbook closes (a7e557b0,
  4818896e, 14e39d13 digests rate them 5/5 with zero friction); `bd remember`
  knowledge capture appears in nearly every substantive session and measurably
  paid out within the window (the /tmp-quota memory, filed 07-24, was already
  guiding sessions on 07-25).
- **The improvement arc.** Within 72 hours: merge-collision → patrol built,
  reviewed cross-vendor, hardened, universally adopted; `bd prime` truncation
  caused a profile regression → root-caused → `.beads/PRIME.md` override halved
  prime output; dependabot vendorHash churn → root-cause grouping config
  (PR 5038) instead of one-by-one merges; rigid-checklist anchoring → "floor
  not ceiling" hygiene doctrine in AGENTS.md. The machinery's failure→fix loop
  is functioning at high velocity.

## Fix/tuning opportunities

### 1. pr-babysit: transient states are treated as terminal (P1, new)

Patrol-log forensics across the window:

| block reason | count | nature |
|---|---:|---|
| `Merge state is UNKNOWN` | 60 | **transient** — GitHub computes mergeability lazily |
| Base branch CI is RED | 67 | correct stop-the-line |
| DIRTY / merge conflicts | 80 | genuine, needs an agent |
| `Merge state is UNSTABLE` | 4 | often transient |

One `UNKNOWN` sighting at patrol time → bead relabeled `merge-blocked` +
unclaimed → tail permanently out of automation, for a state that typically
resolves in under a minute (verified case: mybd-340o / PR 5022, blocked at
15:40Z on `Merge state is UNKNOWN` while base was green). The patrol runs
every 12 minutes — it could simply retain such beads and re-check.

Compounding it: when red-base storms end (main went green 21:02Z tonight),
nothing re-arms the tails that were kicked out during the storm. **18 beads
sit in `merge-blocked` right now.** And nine branches log
`no checks reported on the '<branch>' branch` every 12 minutes, forever —
no-check PRs neither merge nor escalate. Patrol log lines are also
untimestamped raw preflight dumps (459 lines on 07-24 alone), which made this
forensics harder than it should be.

Filed: patrol hardening bead + an immediate re-arm sweep bead (see Follow-ups).

### 2. Delegation debris starves the host (P1, enforcement gap open)

Two hard incidents on 07-24, same class — background delegate work exhausting
a shared host resource:

- **fd exhaustion** (claude/d41b072b): Bash tool unable to spawn *any* process
  for ~45 min; 20+ concurrent background tasks plus leaked embedded-Dolt test
  servers. The zombie-server fix (mybd-q6cz) closed at 17:23Z that day — the
  incident hit 18:46Z, so either the fix wasn't in the running binary or fd
